name: measuretwice-conformance
description: Shared cross-language conformance fixtures for the portable contracts in contracts/v0. Every wrapper runs every group through the Rust core. The fixtures are mandatory for the TypeScript SDK and for the later Python SDK.

groups.runner: Validate each file as one definition artifact. Compare canonical content and hashes with the hashing group.
Reject each raw artifact with the stated reason code and field path, before any evaluator runs.
Validate each input object against its root schema in the Rust core. Materialize the described oversized inputs as stated in their notes.

covers: valid records with labels, groups, tags, and provenance
metadata population, sampling, revision, and label guidelines
groups.runner: Load each valid dataset through the Rust core with the named definition file, then validate every input object. Reject each invalid metadata artifact or record set with the stated reason code and field path. Materialize the stated oversized record as its note describes.
Canonicalize each value in the Rust core and compare the canonical text and the digest. The record shape follows contracts/v0/hashing.schema.json.
Assess each record with the Rust exact rules and compare the outcome and, for maxLength, the code point count.
Reject each text or byte string with the stated reason code. No hash of invalid content is published.
Convert each TypeBox source with the documented conversion, validate it, and compare the canonical content and the definition-domain hash with the named definition file.
Serialize and parse each value and compare the canonical form. Reject each authoring kind with nonportable_value before serialization.
Validate each assessment against the assessment contract and the using list of its check.

Drive each case through the wrapper test adapters and the dispatch contract. Compare the normalized execution, the failure code, and the message fragment, and observe the stated delays through one injected sleep. Decide each label-rule row with the separately specified rule. Verify that replacing the evaluator changes no request field and no definition hash, and that one rebound profile needs its own binding and its own content hash.

covers: mass sum checked by the core
operational record with model, usage, and adapter-measured latency
groups.runner: Drive each case through the Jev adapter and the dispatch contract with one injected clock and one fake call boundary. Compare the normalized assessment, the failure code, the message fragment, and the record fields. Every response of one case comes from the provider fixture of the same name, so every wrapper normalizes the same shapes. The later Python adapter must pass the same cases.

Translate each referenced question check with the versioned Jev translation and compare the complete translated question, the canonical text, and the translation-domain digest through the Rust core. Build the request state from the projected inputs and the using list, and reject every state that carries one field outside the using list. Verify that each identity variant changes the digest, so one changed translated question changes the evaluator binding that records it.

covers: case references with and without one host snapshot reference
no raw case content and no credential in report data
groups.runner: Build one report for each table row and compare the aggregate outcome. Check each sample record against the run report contract. Parse each valid case reference through the case reference boundary and refuse each invalid one with the stated reason code and field path, materializing the stated size tokens.
Validate each artifact, verify each self-hash, and check each compatibility pairing before execution.
Replay each trace through the wrapper scheduler with the fake clock and compare every expected check record, the aggregate outcome, the completion status, and the rejected events.
